agent.result:
Done. `add` and `remove` are now one `set` command:

- `src/commands/set_command.rs` — new module implementing `run_set`: no name → `set needs a name`; name only → clears the note, answering `cleared <name>` or `no note named <name>`; name + value → stores it, answering `set <name>`.
- `src/registry.rs` — dispatches `set`/`list`; unknown commands (including `add`/`remove`) fall through to usage, now `usage: notes [set|list]`.
- `src/commands/mod.rs` — declares `set_command` instead of `add_command`/`remove_command`.
- `tests/cli.rs` — rewritten to cover set/clear/no-name/unknown-name/usage, plus a test confirming `add` and `remove` now hit the usage fallback.

All 6 tests pass (`cargo test`, using `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$TMPDIR/...` since the sandbox blocks writes to a fresh `target/` in the repo root).

One thing to flag: the sandbox also blocked deleting/renaming `src/commands/add_command.rs` and `remove_command.rs` (unlink/rename both returned "Operation not permitted", even with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`). Since `mod.rs` no longer declares them, they're dead code either way, so I emptied their contents — but the files themselves still physically exist in the tree. If you want them actually gone, you'll need to remove them outside this sandbox (e.g. `rm src/commands/add_command.rs src/commands/remove_command.rs` from a normal shell).
